{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABfVq9Fg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzhIzbec", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 380, "title": "Make AI graph node labels function-first, with an AI icon and secondary model details", "body": "## Goal

Rename/relabel **all existing AI-backed graph nodes** so a user can recognize **what the node does before needing to know any model names**.

Use a consistent **AI indicator (sparkles icon) + function-first title**, with the concrete model name as **secondary, smaller text** in the graph canvas and the Add Node palette, and as an explicit read-only field in the node's **Settings** inspector.

This is a **presentation/UX change**, not model selection, runtime refactoring, or a change in which AI models are available.

## Current behavior / problem

In [`extension/graph.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/extension/graph.js), most AI `NODE_TYPES` use model-first labels like `ReazonSpeech ja-en ASR`, `OPUS-MT Japanese → English`, `Kokoro TTS`, etc. Readers unfamiliar with the model names cannot immediately identify the purpose of a node.

The Graph Editor [`extension/graph-editor.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/extension/graph-editor.js) uses `definition.label` in the canvas, Add Node palette, and selected-node inspector. The UI should distinguish function, AI-ness, and implementation model **without conflating these dimensions**.

There are **15 primary model catalog entries** but **16 AI-backed Node types**, because TranslateGemma has separate Japanese→English and English→Japanese node types.

## Proposed display model

For AI-backed nodes:

- **Primary title:** human-readable *operation/function*, e.g. `Speech Recognition · JA/EN`, `Translation · JA → EN`, `Text Summarization`, `Condition Check · Yes/No`, `Speech Synthesis`.
- **AI indicator:** small shared sparkles icon next to the primary title in graph nodes and Add Node results. Non-AI processors/sources/outputs must **not** receive this marker. Make the indicator understandable to assistive technology (accessible label/name); don't rely on color or icon alone.
- **Secondary subtitle:** actual pinned model name in smaller, quieter text, e.g. `ReazonSpeech ja-en` or `Qwen3.5 2B`, on the canvas and in Add Node. Duplicate function titles are intentional and distinguishable by this subtitle; no invented model nicknames or opaque numbered variants.
- **Settings inspector:** selected AI node displays its primary functional title, read-only **Model** (precise model name), **Languages** when meaningful, and **Runtime** (e.g. CPU / WASM or WebGPU) using truthful model-specific values. Keep user-editable settings beneath these facts, not duplicated.
- Do not write `AI` into every visible title: the consistent icon already conveys that. Keep the layout compact and respect node width, text wrapping, focus, selection, keyboard operation, and readability.
- The **Add Node AI Models categories** from #362 must remain intact, including alphabetical / Japanese gojūon sorting (sort by primary functional title, then secondary model name as a stable tie-breaker). Non-AI node names and categories stay as they are.

## Exact 16-node naming proposal

| Existing internal type (must remain unchanged) | New primary display name | Secondary model name |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SpeechToTextReazonSpeech` | **Speech Recognition · JA/EN** | ReazonSpeech ja-en |
| `SpeechToTextWhisper` | **Speech Recognition · Multilingual** | Whisper tiny (multilingual) |
| `SpeechToTextZipformerEn` | **Speech Recognition · EN / Streaming** | Zipformer English |
| `SpeechToTextParakeetV3` | **Speech Recognition** | Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 |
| `SpeechToTextMoonshineMediumEn` | **Speech Recognition · EN / Streaming** | Moonshine Medium Streaming English |
| `OpusMtJaEn` | **Translation · JA → EN** | OPUS-MT |
| `OpusMtEnJa` | **Translation · EN → JA** | OPUS-MT |
| `TranslateGemmaJaEn` | **Translation · JA → EN** | TranslateGemma 4B |
| `TranslateGemmaEnJa` | **Translation · EN → JA** | TranslateGemma 4B |
| `TextSummaryLfm2` | **Text Summarization** | LFM2.5 1.2B JP |
| `TextSummaryQwen35` | **Text Summarization** | Qwen3.5 2B |
| `IfCondition` | **Condition Check · Yes/No** | XtremeDistil |
| `Kokoro` | **Speech Synthesis** | Kokoro 82M |
| `Supertonic3` | **Speech Synthesis** | Supertonic 3 |
| `Qwen3TtsStreaming` | **Speech Synthesis · Streaming** | Qwen3-TTS 0.6B CustomVoice |
| `CosyVoice3Streaming` | **Speech Synthesis · Streaming** | CosyVoice3 0.5B |

Notes:

- Language/streaming text in the primary title should describe **actual model behavior**, not an invented capability. Whisper's `language` port defaults to English and accepts `en`/`ja`; show supported languages accurately in Settings. ReazonSpeech ja-en does not require a language-selection input.
- Models with identical primary titles (e.g. both summary models, both TTS models, both English streaming ASRs, and competing translation models) must remain **individually discoverable** via the persistent secondary model label.
- Use sensible short labels and ellipsis/wrapping rather than forcing unusually wide nodes.

## Implementation guidelines

1. Prefer a clean **separation of presentation metadata** (functional label, model display name, AI marker, language, runtime) from the stable internal node type and inference configuration. Reuse one metadata source in the canvas, Add Node, and inspector, rather than separate hardcoded mappings that drift.
2. Update all Graph Editor surfaces that render a node name, including search results, inspector, accessible labels, tooltips and relevant diagnostics, so function-first labels are understandable. Search should still match the **model name** (`ReazonSpeech`, `Kokoro`, etc.) as well as the function name.
3. Preserve existing ports, edges, parameter settings, graph validation, Auto Save, model asset requirements, model licenses and loading, and the execution runtime. **Do not rename internal `node.type` strings**, migrate saved graphs, or change persisted JSON solely for the UI relabeling.
4. Keep the icon implementation consistent with the project's current lightweight UI. No external icon download or new icon dependency is necessary.
5. Preserve normal (non-AI) node labels and UI behavior. Existing Speaker, Text, TextFormatter, Display, processors and graph/subgraph UI should not be accidentally marked as AI.
6. Maintain the distinction between **model-name details and editable runtime settings**; showing a Model field must not imply that a user can switch the model within the same Node type.
7. Update related documentation, palette screenshots/fixtures and accessibility expectations where affected.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All **16 AI-backed Node types** use the exact or semantically equivalent **function-first** primary names above across canvas and Add Node.
- [ ] Each is visibly identified as AI by a consistent small icon, with an accessible alternative; non-AI Nodes are not marked as AI.
- [ ] Each shows its precise model name as a **smaller secondary label** in canvas and Add Node.
- [ ] When an AI Node is selected, **Settings** contains read-only **Model**, supported **Languages** where applicable, and **Runtime**, all truthful to that model; actual editable settings remain unchanged.
- [ ] Name collisions are handled cleanly: users can tell OPUS-MT from TranslateGemma, LFM2.5 from Qwen3.5, Qwen3-TTS from CosyVoice3, etc.
- [ ] Add Node remains sorted in its existing categories; text search finds AI Nodes by task **and by model name**.
- [ ] Save/import/export and execution of existing graphs remain byte-compatible in their schema / stable type IDs, including ports, model cache preparation and Graph Library.
- [ ] Keyboard navigation, selection, focus, screen-reader labels, and small graph cards remain usable.
- [ ] Add automated unit/UI regression tests for metadata, collision handling, sorting, searching, inspector details, accessibility and serialized graph compatibility. No human approval gate.

## Out of scope

- Changing AI model selections or pruning the catalog.
- Adding a generic model registry or dynamic model switching.
- Changing the Models page or standalone model Playground.
- Refactoring inference workers or changing how model files are downloaded.
